explanation: His Bible of the 1450s was printed in about 180 copies, of which 49 survive. By 1500, presses were working in more than 200 European towns.

claims.text: Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith of Mainz, developed a printing press with movable metal type around 1440.
William Caxton printed in England from the 1470s, Aldus Manutius in Venice from the 1490s, and Albrecht Dürer was a Nuremberg artist and printmaker; none developed the Mainz press.
The Gutenberg Bible, printed in the 1450s, had an edition of about 180 copies.
About 49 copies of the Gutenberg Bible survive, complete or in part.
By 1500, printing presses were operating in more than 200 European towns.

issues.note: The stem says 'Around 1440, which goldsmith in Mainz'. Around 1440 Gutenberg was working in Strasbourg and he was back in Mainz by about 1448, so 'goldsmith from Mainz' would be exact. The key is unaffected.
